record_only.summary: Empiric antibiotic therapy was started for a presumed bacterial urinary/allograft process while microbiologic tests were pending; the patient initially improved.
record_only.temporality: early hospitalization before hospital day 3 worsening

record_only.summary: The source interprets the renal biopsy findings as characteristic of adenovirus infection and notes immunohistochemical confirmation. The interpretive disease wording is not rankable; only raw biopsy and test observations are listed above.
After diagnostic testing, cidofovir with probenecid was given and immunosuppression was decreased.

The article reports clearance of viremia in 29 days, stopping cidofovir after the viral load became undetectable, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL at treatment completion, no urine protein isolate, rapid symptom resolution, and improved renal function.
record_only.temporality: after treatment initiation through treatment completion

record_only.summary: Retrospective neutralization testing showed Patient 1 was seronegative before transplant and seroconverted after transplant; donor and Patient 2 serology are used in the article to discuss possible transmission timing.

The donor was a 31-year-old male with seizure, head trauma, arrest, no noted respiratory illness, sinus CT changes, transient chest x-ray opacity, and later donor-serum evidence of prior HAdV-34 exposure. This is source/epidemiologic context, not Patient 1 presentation evidence.

Patient 2, the other kidney recipient, is described separately with fever, chills, malaise, tachycardia, laboratory abnormalities, E. coli cultures, negative serum adenovirus nucleic acid testing, and later seroconversion. This is not part of the selected Patient 1 case.
Discussion statements about donor-derived infection probability, adenovirus latency, environmental acquisition, rarity, and screening recommendations are excluded from ranking.
The title and abstract contain the article-level diagnostic framing and are preserved only as citation metadata, not as case evidence.
